วันนี้ (๒๑ ส.ค. ๖๓) เวลา ๙.๐๐ น. นายอนุช: Today (21 Aug 2020) at 9:00 a.m., Mr. Anucha Nakasai, Minister attached to the Prime Minister's Office, visited the Office of the Royal Society to attend a meeting of the sub-committee
ภาพประกอบข่าว รัฐมนตรีประจำสำนักนายกรัฐม: News image: Minister attached to the Prime Minister's Office visits and gives policy guidance to the Office of the Royal Society
นายอนุชา นาคาศัย รัฐมนตรีประจำสำนักนายกร: Mr. Anucha Nakasai, Minister attached to the Prime Minister's Office, said that the Office of the Royal Society is an important agency that contributes greatly to the nation. Its academic work is not limited to language alone; many of its academic works serve as references for current research and can be used for work, study and academic citation. It preserves the Thai language sustainably, coins new terms, develops the language and passes this heritage on to future generations, transferring knowledge from the present generation to the next, including training in Thai and local dialects in each region. To ensure smooth operations, he asked the executives to plan for an adequate workforce structure and to set up information technology database systems so that both Office of the Royal Society premises can work together in a coordinated and unified manner. This is a good opportunity for the Royal Society of Thailand to transform its image into a modern digital government agency, moving into the Government 4.0 era with a focus on convenience for the public. For example, an application could let the public find the locations of both Royal Society service points, navigate to them, access a service guide and rate their satisfaction after receiving services. This responds to government policy: on 16 June 2020 the Cabinet approved, in line with the opinion of the Bureau of the Budget, funding to renovate the Chao Chom Manda Luean building into the Royal Society of Thailand History Hall, and the contract is expected to be signed before the end of September 2020.
รัฐมนตรีประจำสำนักนายกรัฐมนตรี กล่าวเพิ่: The Minister attached to the Prime Minister's Office added that the Office of the Royal Society has always served as the principal organization for preserving and promoting the use of the Thai language. Its activities, such as Thai language skills competitions for young people and awards for outstanding users of Thai, are good projects that build competitiveness and strengthen human potential. Today is a highly competitive digital age; if the Office of the Royal Society adds online sales channels for its academic works or produces e-books, it will reduce paper use, offer greater convenience and speed, meet public needs and adapt to Government 4.0, or a digital-era government focused on public convenience. It should develop into a modern service organization, honor the Fellows of the Royal Society as revered persons of the nation to inspire young people with good role models, become a source of accurate knowledge and understanding about the monarchy and royal duties, and add more channels for academic services so the public can access them more easily.
